title: Omega-3 and DHA in Pregnancy: Food Sources and Supplement Cautions
excerpt: The role of DHA, low-mercury fish options, and when to ask a clinician about supplements.
content:
## Introduction to Omega-3 and DHA
Omega-3 and DHA are two essential fatty acids that play a crucial role in the diet of pregnant women. DHA (docosahexaenoic acid) is a type of omega-3 fatty acid that is important for the development of the fetus, particularly in the formation of the brain and nervous system.

## The Role of DHA in Pregnancy
DHA supports the development of the brain, vision, and nervous system of the fetus. Additionally, DHA may help reduce the risk of preterm birth and other pregnancy-related complications. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), pregnant women should consume at least 200mg of DHA per day.

## Food Sources of Omega-3 and DHA
There are several food sources that are rich in Omega-3 and DHA, including:
* Fatty fish: Fatty fish like salmon, sardines, and anchovies are rich in DHA and omega-3.
* Shellfish: Shellfish like mussels and oysters are also good sources of DHA and omega-3.
* Fortified foods: Some foods like eggs, yogurt, and infant formula are fortified with DHA and omega-3.
* Algal oil: Algal oil is a vegetarian source of DHA and omega-3.

## Fish Consumption and Mercury Levels
When consuming fish, pregnant women need to be aware of the mercury levels in the fish. Fish with high levels of mercury can harm the development of the fetus. According to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), pregnant women should limit their consumption of fish with high levels of mercury like shark, swordfish, and king mackerel.

## Omega-3 and DHA Supplements
Omega-3 and DHA supplements can be an option for pregnant women who are unable to get enough DHA from food sources. However, before taking supplements, pregnant women should consult with their healthcare provider about the appropriate dosage and type of supplement. According to the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), pregnant women should choose supplements that contain DHA and omega-3 from fish or algal oil.

## Conclusion
Omega-3 and DHA are essential fatty acids that play a crucial role in the diet of pregnant women. Pregnant women should consume enough DHA from food sources and limit their consumption of fish with high levels of mercury. If supplements are necessary, pregnant women should consult with their healthcare provider about the appropriate dosage and type of supplement. For more information on pregnancy nutrition and meal planning, visit our [pregnancy meal planner](/planner) or [read more about prenatal nutrition](/blog/prenatal-nutrition).

## When to Consult a Healthcare Provider
Pregnant women should consult with their healthcare provider about:
* The appropriate dosage and type of omega-3 and DHA supplements
* Safe fish consumption during pregnancy
* Other food sources of omega-3 and DHA
